MAJAZ:v1p14/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r8.claim: The lām is understood but omitted in كالوهم and وزنوهم: ‘when they measure or weigh for them.’
MAJAZ:v1p14/r8.anchor: قال: «ويل للمطففين الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون» (83/ 3) معناه: وإذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم.

BURHAN:v2p7/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p7/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p7/r6.claim: Most future-tense conditional responses are general, as in the examples of cheating in measure, mocking, and arrogance.
BURHAN:v2p7/r6.anchor: وإن كان مستقبلا فأكثر موارده للعموم كقوله ﴿ وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون ﴾

ITQAN:v2p533#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p533#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p533#3/r6.claim: هم is not an emphatic nominative pronoun for the wāw; the rasm has no alif after either wāw, so هم is the object.
ITQAN:v2p533#3/r6.anchor: ومن قال في ﴿ وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون ﴾ إن هم ضمير رفع مؤكد للواو

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.claim: The relative clause explains how the cheaters shortchange others and why they merit condemnation: when receiving measured goods in a purchase, they take the full amount and more.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.anchor: صفة كاشفة للمطففين شارحة لكيفية تطفيفهم الذي استحقوا به الذم

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r4.claim: When they measure or weigh goods for others, the original preposition meaning ‘for’ is omitted and the verb takes the object directly.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r4.anchor: أي وإذا كالوا للناس أو وزنوا لهم المبيع ونحوه

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r5.claim: The attached pronoun is accusative as the object, not nominative emphasis on the plural verb; Quranic spelling and comparison with other plural forms support that parsing.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r5.anchor: فلفظ هم منصوب المحل على المفعولية لا مرفوعة على التأكيد للواو

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r6.claim: Yukhsirun means they reduce others’ rights, contrary to the purpose of measures and scales, which is equality and justice.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r6.anchor: أي ينقصون حقوقهم مع إن وضع الكيل والوزن إنما هو للتسوية والتعديل

QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.claim: Beyond literal cheating in measures, the verses concern cheating on the true scale of justice, where character and deeds are measured.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يحمل بعد الظاهر على التطفيف في الميزان الحقيقي الذي هو العدل، والموزونات به هي الأخلاق والأعمال

QASHANI:83:1-5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r3.claim: They undervalue others' virtues through arrogance and love of superiority; Qashani links this to 3:188.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r3.anchor: اعتبروا كمالات الناس بالنسبة إلى كمالاتهم أخسروها واستحقروها ولم يراعوا العدالة

AKHFASH:v2p572/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p572/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p572/r1.claim: كالوهم وزنوهم means measuring or weighing people; Hijazi usage says كِلْت زيدا and وزنتُه for doing so on his behalf.
AKHFASH:v2p572/r1.anchor: [183 ب] قال {وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون} أي: "اذا كالوا الناس أووزنوهم" لأن أهل الحجاز يقولون "كلت زيدا" و"وزنته" أي: "كلت له" و"وزنت له".

FARRA:v3p245#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p245#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p245#2/r3.claim: In كالوهم/وزنوهم the suffix is an accusative object with a benefactive sense, equivalent to measured for them; a Hijazi Bedouin woman's usage confirms it.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r1.claim: كالوهم and وزنوهم mean they measured or weighed for them; Arabic uses the recipient suffix directly where لك is meant.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r1.anchor: يقال: كلتك ووزنتك؛ بمعنى: كلت لك

MAJAZ:v2p289/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p289/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p289/r2.claim: كالوهم and وزنوهم mean measured or weighed for them; Khuffāf's poetry witnesses the construction.
MAJAZ:v2p289/r2.anchor: «وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم» (3) إذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

MAJAZ:v2p289/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p289/r3.speaker: خفاف
MAJAZ:v2p289/r3.claim: Khuffāf's verse is cited as evidence for the object suffix in the meaning “for them.”
MAJAZ:v2p289/r3.anchor: قال خفاف: يصيدك قافلا والمخ رار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r2.claim: In kālūhum and wazanūhum the sellers are subjects and “them” refers to customers; the construction omits the prepositional lām from kālū lahum and wazanū lahum.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r2.anchor: فالواوان من { كالوهم أو وزنوهم } عائدان إلى اسم الموصول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r3.claim: Since kāla and wazana normally take a measured object, omitting the lām is a frequent lightening of “measure/weigh for them,” like common verbs such as thanking someone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r3.anchor: ولكثرة دورانه على اللسان خففوه فقالوا : كاله ووزنه طعاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the people of the Ḥijāz and nearby Qays say “measure for us” as well as “measure for them”; others use the direct-object construction only.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r4.anchor: قال الفراء : هو من كلام أهل الحجاز ومن جاورهم من قيس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.claim: The buyers' side mentions measuring alone because they usually bought produce by measure and paid in weighed coin; sellers use both measure and weight, revealing that the cheating was merchants' practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.anchor: فلذلك اقتصر في ابتياعهم من الجالبين على الاكتيال نظرا إلى الغالب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r2.claim: Yukhsirūn means they cause their customers to incur a monetary loss by shorting a transaction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r2.anchor: ومعنى { يخسرون } يوقعون الذين كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم في الخسارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.claim: The passage warns Muslims against widespread short-measure practices in early Medina and condemns the polytheists of Medina and Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية تحذير للمسلمين من التساهل في التطفيف إذ وجوده فاشيا في المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.claim: Short measure combines injustice, theft, and meanness, traits the Arabs disdained separately yet practiced together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.anchor: أن التطفيف يجمع ظلما واختلاسا ولؤما

NAHHAS:v5p173/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
NAHHAS:v5p173/r8.claim: Most grammarians, including Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, al-Kisaʾi, and al-Akhfash, parse the attached pronouns as accusative objects, following Sibawayh’s analogy with كَلْتُكَ and صَدْتُكَ.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r8.anchor: قال جلتهم أبو عمرو بن العلاء والكسائي والأخفش وغيرهم موضع الهاء والميم موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v5p173/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r9.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
NAHHAS:v5p173/r9.claim: Isa ibn Umar parses the pronouns as nominative: they themselves make the measure or weight deficient, beginning a new clause after كالوا.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r9.anchor: وقال عيسى بن عمر الهاء والميم في موضع رفع وعبر عنه أبو حاتم بأن المعنى عنده هم إذا كالوا

NAHHAS:v5p173/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
NAHHAS:v5p173/r10.claim: Isa ibn Umar’s pause places a stop after كالوا, then begins the subject هم before أو وزنوا.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r10.anchor: لأن عيسى قال الوقف وإذا كالوا ثم تبتدىء هم أو وزنوا

NAHHAS:v5p173/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r11.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p173/r11.claim: Another analysis treats هم as an emphatic pronoun, as in قاموا هم.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r11.anchor: وعبر غيره أن هم توكيد كما تقول قاموا هم

NAHHAS:v5p173/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r12.claim: Nahhas prefers accusative: the written form lacks an alif, and the sequence requires وإذا كالوا لهم, with the preposition لام omitted.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r12.anchor: والصواب أن الهاء والميم في موضع نصب لأنه في السواد بغير ألف ونسق الكلام يدل على ذلك

NAHHAS:v5p173/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r13.speaker: أبو زيد
NAHHAS:v5p173/r13.claim: Abu Zayd’s verse جنيتك أكموءا وعساقلا illustrates deleting a preposition with a verb taking a direct and a prepositional object.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r13.anchor: كما قال أنشده أبو زيد ( ولقد جنيتك أكموءا وعساقلا

NAHHAS:v5p173/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r14.claim: Other cited poetry illustrates omitted prepositions with two-object verbs, including أمرتك الخير, نبيت عبد الله, and أستغفر الله ذنبا; the poets are unnamed here.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r14.anchor: ( أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به … فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r10.claim: Isa ibn ʿUmar separates the verbs and pauses after each: sellers shortchange when they themselves weigh or measure; Hamza transmits this reading, with هم reinforcing the pronoun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r10.anchor: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلها حرفين ويقف على «كالوا» و «وزنوا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r12.claim: يخسرون is a causative form, both خسر and أخسر can mean to reduce or spoil, and the object of كالوهم is omitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r12.anchor: ويخسرون معدى بالهمزة يقال: خسر الرجل وأخسره غيره، والمفعول ل كالوهم محذوف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r1.claim: “When they measure or weigh for them,” the defrauders reduce the amount; on this parsing, “hum” is the object and one should not pause after “measured.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r1.anchor: أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوهم أي وزنوا لهم يخسرون أي ينقصون في الكيل والوزن فعلى هذا لا يجوز أن يقف على كالوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r2.claim: An alternative takes “hum” as an emphatic pronoun, allowing a pause after “measured.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من يجعل هم توكيدا لما كالوا ويجوز أن يقف على كالوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r3.claim: The author prefers the first grammatical analysis, where “hum” is the object pronoun and one does not pause after “measured.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r4.speaker: امرأة أعرابية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a Bedouin woman’s line as evidence for the idiom of measuring out to someone, including the form “kīl lanā.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r4.anchor: قال الفراء سمعت أعرابية تقول إذا صدر الناس أتينا التاجر فيكليلنا

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.claim: The common reading joins “they measure for them” as a transitive construction, with “them” as the object; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar instead pauses after “they measure” and starts “they are defrauders” with “they” as subject, a reading attributed to Ḥamzah.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة: (كالوهم أو وزنوهم) متصلا بغير ألف، ولا وقف بين (كالوا)، وبين (هم).

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.claim: The author prefers the joined reading because the written form lacks an alif, Arabic says “I measured your due” meaning “for you,” and the readers unanimously use it.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.anchor: والأوجه الأول لوجوه: أحدها: أنهم كتبوها بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.claim: Ṭafīf means tiny or insignificant; a mutaffif reduces another person's proper measure or weight, whether by a small shortfall or a subtle theft.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.anchor: الطفيف: الشيء التفه القليل، والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحبه بنقصانه

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.claim: One explanation names the act for the tiny amount missing from the rightful measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأن ما ينقص منه طفيف قليل

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.claim: Another view calls the act a secret theft of a small amount.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.anchor: وقيل: التطفيف: أن يسرق الشيء اليسير في خفية

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.claim: Related usage describes an underfilled vessel and says all descendants of Adam are close to a full measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.anchor: وإناء طفان إذا لم يكن ملآن، ومنه: بنو آدم كلهم طف الصاع

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.claim: No one has superiority over another except through piety.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.anchor: فليس لأحد على أحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r14.claim: In kaluhum and wazanuhum, the pronoun refers to people as direct objects, with the preposition removed and the verb made transitive; cited poetry likewise uses the verb for someone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r14.anchor: وفيه وجهان : أن يراد كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم ؛ فحذف الجار وأوصل الفعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r1.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun stands for the omitted measured or weighed amount, with the genitive noun taking its place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r1.anchor: وأن يكون على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه ، والمضاف هو المكيل أو الموزون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r2.claim: He rejects making the pronoun the subject referring to the cheaters: that reverses the point from how they treat recipients to who performs the act, producing incoherent discourse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r2.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون ضميرا مرفوعا للمطففين ، لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r3.claim: He also rejects relying on the mushaf's omission of the alif after plural waw to rule out the subject reading; orthography is not consistently conventional and the alif is not pronounced or meaningful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r3.anchor: والتعلق في إيطاله بخط المصحف ، وأن الألف التي تكتب بعد واو الجمع غير ثابتة فيه : ركيك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r4.claim: The alif after plural waw merely distinguishes it visually from a singular verb, and some scribes omit it because context already distinguishes the forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r4.anchor: وإنما كتبت هذه الألف تفرقة بين واو الجمع وغيرها في نحو قولك : هم لم يدعوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r5.speaker: عيسى بن عمر، حمزة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r5.claim: Isa ibn Umar and Hamza do read the pronouns as referring to the cheaters, pausing at both waw letters to make their reading clear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r5.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر وحمزة : أنهما كانا يرتكبان ذلك ، أي يجعلان الضميرين للمطففين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r6.claim: They likely buy only by measure, since it lets them steal by manipulating how full the measure is; when giving, either measure or weight lets them shortchange.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r6.anchor: كأن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r7.claim: Yukhsirun means they diminish the amount; one says a scale loses or causes a loss.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r7.anchor: يخسرون } ينقصون يقال : خسر الميزان وأخسره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r10.speaker: الفضيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r10.claim: Al-Fudayl says shortchanging the scale blackens one's face on the Day of Resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r10.anchor: وعن الفضيل : بخس الميزان سواد الوجه يوم القيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r11.speaker: عبد الملك بن مروان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r11.claim: A Bedouin rebuked Abd al-Malik: if cheaters face this threat, what of a ruler taking Muslims' property without measuring it?
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r11.anchor: فما ظنك بنفسك وأنت تأخذ أموال المسلمين بلا كيل ولا وزن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r12.claim: The second verb omits لهم because the intended sense, measuring or weighing for them, is clear; the cheater gives them less than due.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r12.anchor: يعني كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم بحذف هذه الكلمة لما في الكلام من الدلالة عليها

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.claim: A report about the pre-Islamic market says buyers received extra measure while sellers gave short measure, using two measures and two scales and shifting between them.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.anchor: وكان بسوق الجاهلية لهم كيلين وميزانين معلومة لا يعاب عليهم فيها

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r5.claim: He glosses their loss when measuring or weighing for others as giving them less than their due.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r5.anchor: فقال: { الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون } [آية: 3] يعني ينقصون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r1.claim: The object pronoun refers to people; the phrasing means they measure or weigh for them, omitting the preposition and making the verb transitive.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r1.anchor: والضمير المنصوب فى ﴿ وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم ﴾ راجع إلى الناس أى كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم فحذف الجار واوصل الفعل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r2.claim: They may measure incoming goods because measuring lets them exploit the filling and steal, while weighing allows similar manipulation; when giving out goods they use both measures.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r3.claim: Yukhsirūn means they reduce what they give; one says that a scale has lost weight or that someone has made it short.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r3.anchor: ﴿ يخسرون ﴾ ينقصون يقال خسر الميزان واخسره

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r4.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Farra read “measure or weigh them” as “measure or weigh for them,” with the preposition omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r4.anchor: أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم فحذفت اللام، فتعدى الفعل فنصب

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r5.claim: Al-Farra cites a Hijazi woman's wording to illustrate the verb: a merchant measures two units for us.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: وسمعت أعرابية تقول إذا صدر الناس أتينا التاجر فيكيلنا المد والمدين

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r6.speaker: الزجاج والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Kisaʾi require joining the attached hum pronoun to the verb rather than pausing after kalu or wazanu.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: لا يجوز الوقف على «كالوا» و «ووزنوا» حتى تصل به «هم»

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r7.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar treated hum as a separate emphatic word and paused; he thinks Hamzah may have read likewise.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلها حرفين، ويقف على «كالوا» و «وزنوا»

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r8.claim: Abu ʿUbayd prefers treating verbs and pronoun as one word because of the spelling and Arabic transitive usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: والاختيار أن يكونا كلمة واحدة من جهتين: إحداهما: الخط

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r9.claim: On the common reading, hum is an accusative object referring to people, either with an omitted preposition or omitted noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r9.anchor: على قراءة العامة، راجع إلى الناس، تقديره «وإذا كالوا» الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r10.claim: Yakhsirun means to reduce or make the measure come up short.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r10.anchor: قوله: { يخسرون }: أي ينقصون والعرب تقول: أخسرت الميزان وخسرته

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.claim: A Prophetic warning pairs five wrongs with consequences: broken covenants bring enemies, rejecting God's law poverty, immorality plague, short measure drought, and withholding alms the loss of rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.anchor: خمس بخمس: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits the warning by gist, and Malik also relates it from Ibn ʿUmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.anchor: خرجه أبو بكر البزار بمعناه، ومالك بن أنس أيضا من حديث ابن عمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.claim: Malik ibn Dinar tells of a dying neighbor who used two measures and saw them grow into mountains of fire when struck together.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: دخلت على جار لي قد نزل به الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.claim: ʿIkrimah swears every measurer or weigher is destined for Hell, even when asked whether this applies to his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أشهد على كل كيال أو وزان أنه في النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Asmaʿi quotes a Bedouin saying manliness cannot reside in measure rims or scale tongues; it is also related from ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.anchor: قال الأصمعي: وسمعت أعرابية تقول: لا تلتمس المروءة ممن مروءته

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.speaker: عبد خير
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.claim: ʿAbd Khayr says ʿAli overturned a scale that gave excess saffron, ordering accurate weight first and voluntary excess afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.anchor: وقال عبد خير: مر علي رضي الله عنه على رجل وهو يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.claim: Nafiʿ says Ibn ʿUmar warned short-measurers will stand in sweat up to half their ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.anchor: وقال نافع: كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.claim: Abu Hurayrah says Medina's deputy recited this surah at dawn; he prayed against a trader who bought with full measure but sold short.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.anchor: وقرأ في الركعة الثانية «ويل للمطففين» قال أبو هريرة: فأقول في صلاتي

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r9.claim: The alternative nominative reading is rejected because the first verb would have no predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r9.anchor: ولا يصح لأنه تكون الأولى ملغاة، ليس لها خبر، وإنما كانت تستقيم لو كان بعدها: وإذا كالوا هم ينقصون، أو وزنوا هم يخسرون.

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r1.claim: One parses “they measured them” as “they measured for them,” deleting the preposition and making the verb transitive; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ cite Hijazi usage.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r1.anchor: أن المراد من قوله ( كالوهم أو وزنوهم ) كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم ، فحذف الجار

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r2.claim: A second parse omits a noun and puts its genitive pronoun in its place: they measured or weighed what was due to them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r2.anchor: أن يكون على حذف المضاف ، وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه ، والتقدير : وإذا كالوا مكيلهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وحمزة
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r3.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ḥamzah read the pronouns as emphatic objects attached to the verbs, with a pause at the two wāws.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r3.anchor: يروى عن عيسى بن عمر ، وحمزة أنهما كانا يجعلان الضميرين توكيدا لما في كالوا

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj reject that reading because the written form lacks the expected alif; al-Kashshāf objects that Qurʾānic orthography is not always conventional, but Rāzī says the early spelling practice should have been preserved.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r4.anchor: وزعم الفراء والزجاج أنه غير جائز ، لأنه لو كان بمعنى كالوهم لكان في المصحف ألف مثبتة

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says akhsara al-mīzān and khasara al-mīzān both mean to diminish the balance; al-Muʾarrij says “they diminish” is Qurayshi usage.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج : أخسرت الميزان وخسرته سواء أي نقصته ، وعن المؤرج يخسرون ينقصون بلغة قريش

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.claim: When the Prophet first reached Madinah, its people were notorious defrauders; after revelation of these verses, they weighed honestly.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās said, “When the Prophet first moved to Madinah, its inhabitants were the worst kind of defrauders

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.speaker: Abū Hurayrah
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.claim: The verses refer directly to a man who used separate scales for buying and selling.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.anchor: According to Abū Hurayrah, these verses refer directly to a man who had two scales

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.claim: The Prophet linked covenant-breaking with enemies, judging apart from revelation with poverty, fornication with death, fraud with crop failure and famine, and withholding alms with withheld rain; no grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.anchor: The Prophet recited them to the citizens of Madinah and said, “Five for five.”

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.claim: The warning extends beyond commerce: anyone who intentionally falls short in anything ordained by God may face shame and suffering.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.anchor: shame and suffering will befall anyone who intentionally falls short in any matter according to what has been ordained by God

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r6.claim: A noncanonical reading treats both instances of “them” as subjects rather than direct objects: “when they measure or weigh, they stint.”
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r6.anchor: can be read as an affirmation of

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r1.claim: Because the written form omits the alif after the verb’s plural wāw, the pronoun هم can be accusative, referring to الناس: they measure or weigh the people’s goods.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r1.anchor: هو ضمير نصب، فيكون مفعولا به، ويعود على الناس، أي: وإذا كالوا الناس، أو وزنوا الناس

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r2.claim: On the object-pronoun analysis, the verbs take two objects: one directly and the other through a preposition that may be omitted; scholars differ over which verb is basic.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r2.anchor: الأصل في هذين الفعلين التعدي لاثنين، لأحدهما بنفسه بلا خلاف، وللآخر بحرف الجر، ويجوز حذفه

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī cites the line جنيتك as Arabic evidence for deleting the preposition, with the sense جنيت لك.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r3.anchor:
وأنشد الزمخشري:
4513 ولقد جنيتك أكمؤا وعساقلا

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r4.claim: Alternatively, هم is a nominative pronoun emphasizing the plural wāw and referring to the short-measurers; on this reading, the goods and their recipients are omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r4.anchor: أنه ضمير رفع مؤكد للواو. والضمير عائد على المطففين، ويكون على هذا قد حذف المكيل والمكيل له

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects the nominative reading because it would say they short-measure when acting as measurers themselves, disrupting the contrast between taking from people and giving to them.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r5.anchor: لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد، وذلك أن المعنى: إذا أخذوا من الناس استوفوا، وإذا أعطوهم أخسروا

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r6.claim: The Shaykh denies any incoherence: emphasis does not change the focus on the act, and the recipients of measuring are understood because they would not short themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا تنافر فيه بوجه، ولا فرق بين أن يؤكد الضمير أو لا يؤكد، والحديث واقع في الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r7.claim: Al-Samīn says al-Zamakhsharī’s contrast between taking from others and giving to others is more complete and better, and only the accusative pronoun referring to people yields it.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r7.anchor: ولا شك أن هذا المعنى الذي ذكره الزمخشري وأراده أتم وأحسن من المعنى الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r8.claim: The missing alif after the plural wāw favors the accusative pronoun analysis by indicating its connection to the verb.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r8.anchor: ورجح الأول سقوط الألف بعد الواو، ولأنه دال على اتصال الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls reliance on the muṣḥaf’s spelling weak: its orthography often departs from standard conventions, and some expert manuscripts omit the alif because it is absent from speech and meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r9.anchor: لأن خط المصحف لم يراع في كثير منه حد المصطلح عليه في علم الخط، على أني رأيت في الكتب المخطوطة

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the plural wāw itself conveys plurality; the written alif merely distinguishes it from a nonplural wāw, so context can make it unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r10.anchor: لأن الواو وحدها معطية معنى الجمع، وإنما كتبت هذه الألف تفرقة بين واو الجمع وغيرها

SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r11.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وحمزة
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r11.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ḥamza use the nominative pronouns referring to the short-measurers, pausing after each wāw to show their intended parsing.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3/r11.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر وحمزة أنها يرتكبان ذلك، أي: يجعلان الضميرين للمطففين، ويقفان عند الواوين وقيفة

SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says they took goods by measure alone because measuring let them overfill and steal, but used both measures and scales when giving so they could short either amount.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " كأن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r2.claim: يخسرون answers إذا and is causative, as in خسر الرجل versus أخسرته; its omitted object is الناس متاعهم.
SAMIN-DURR:83:3#2/r2.anchor: جواب " إذا " وهو معدى بالهمزة. يقال: خسر الرجل، وأخسرته أنا، فمفعوله محذوف

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī describes wayl as a valley of Hell’s pus for those who shortchange people in measures and weights, withholding their due full amount; mutaffif comes from something slight or scant.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.anchor: والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحب الحق عما له من الوفاء والتمام في كيل أو وزن؛

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.claim: ʿIkrima swears that every measurer and weigher is in the Fire: none gives the same measure or weight that they themselves demand.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: أشهد أن كل كيال ووزان في النار،

TAB-FULL:v24p186/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r2.claim: When they measure or weigh for others, they shortchange them.
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r2.anchor: وقوله: {وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم} [المطففين: 3] يقول: وإذا هم كالوا للناس أو وزنوا لهم.

TAB-FULL:v24p186/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r3.claim: In Hijazi usage, expressions like weighing someone their due or measuring their food mean weighing or measuring it for that person.
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r3.anchor: ومن لغة أهل الحجاز أن يقولوا: وزنتك حقك، وكلتك طعامك، بمعنى: وزنت لك وكلت لك.

TAB-FULL:v24p186/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r4.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r4.claim: ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar parses hum as a separate nominative subject, pauses after the verbs, and reads the sense as They shortchange.
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r4.anchor: وكان عيسى بن عمر فيما ذكر عنه يجعلهما حرفين، ويقف على كالوا، وعلى وزنوا، ثم يبتدئ: هم يخسرون.

TAB-FULL:v24p186/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers attaching hum to the verbs as their object: the spelling without a separating alif shows it is a connected object pronoun, not a new subject.
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r5.anchor: والصواب في ذلك عندي: الوقف على هم، لأن كالوا ووزنوا لو كانا مكتفيين، وكانت هم كلاما مستأنفا، كانت كتابة كالوا ووزنوا بألف فاصلة

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r8.claim: When they measure or weigh for other people, they reduce the amount given.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r8.anchor: أي إذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم يخسرون، أي ينقصون في الكيل والوزن

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r9.claim: Arabic permits the form yukh'sirūn here, although he knows of no one who recited that form in this place.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r9.anchor: ولا أعلم أحدا قرأ في هذا الموضع يخسرون

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r10.claim: On the preferred parse, the pronoun in kālūhum is an object meaning 'they measured for them'; it must be joined to the verb, so one cannot pause after kālū.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r10.anchor: لم يجز أن يقف على كالوا حتى يصلها ب (هم)

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r11.claim: Some treat hum as emphasis for the subject pronoun in kālū, which would permit pausing after the verb.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r11.anchor: ومن الناس من يجعل " هم " توكيدا لما في كالوا، فيجوز أن تقف

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r12.claim: He prefers parsing hum as an accusative object meaning 'for them'; if it were emphasis, the written text would contain an alif before hum.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r12.anchor: والاختيار أن تكون " هم " في موضع نصب، بمعنى كالوا لهم.

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.claim: The sura opens by warning those who cheat in measure and weight that they will be resurrected for judgment on the Great Day, then describes the fates of wicked and righteous; context suggests the opening was revealed in Medina.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: تفتتح السورة بوعيد أهل التطفيف في الكيل والوزن وتنذرهم بأنهم مبعوثون للجزاء في يوم عظيم وهو يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.claim: They take their full due when buying but reduce what they give when selling, thereby making others lose.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.anchor: والاستيفاء أخذ الحق تاما كاملا، والإخسار الإيقاع في الخسارة. والمعنى الذين إذا أخذوا من الناس بالكيل يأخذون حقهم تاما كاملا،

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.claim: Both verses condemn one wrong: they insist on rights for themselves but deny others equal reciprocal rights, corrupting a society built on balanced claims.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.anchor: الآيتين جميعا ذم واحد وهو أنهم يراعون الحق لأنفسهم ولا يراعونه لغيرهم وبعبارة أخرى لا يراعون لغيرهم من الحق مثل

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.claim: One explanation says only buying by measure is mentioned because dealers commonly bought bulk grain and resold small amounts, usually by measure; the author finds this weak.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.anchor: قيل لأن المطففين كانوا باعة وهم كانوا في الأغلب يشترون الكثير من الحبوب والبقول ونحوهما من الأمتعة ثم يكسبون بها

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.claim: Another says weighing need not be mentioned when buying because weight and measure jointly indicate buying and selling; the author says the reasoning also applies to measures and is arbitrary.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.anchor: وقيل لم يذكر الاتزان لأن الكيل والوزن بهما البيع والشراء فذكر أحدهما يدل على الآخر. وفيه أن ما ذكر في

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.claim: A third explanation says the original cheats bought only by measure but sold by measure and weight; the author calls this an unsupported claim, and finds the other explanations weak too.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.anchor: وقيل الآيتان تحاكيان ما كان عليه دأب الذين نزلت فيهم السورة فقد كانوا يشترون بالاكتيال فقط ويبيعون بالكيل والوزن جميعا،

TABRISI:83:1-3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r5.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
TABRISI:83:1-3/r5.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads the pronoun in “they measure them” as an independent word in nominative position or as emphasis on the subject pronoun.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r5.anchor: عيسى بن عمر يجعل " هم " فصلا في موضع رفع

TABRISI:83:1-3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r6.claim: The other readers' object-pronoun analysis is correct: they measure or weigh for their customers.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r6.anchor: والباقون يجعلونها ضمير المنصوب وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:83:1-3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r7.claim: The Hijaz dialect says “I weighed you your due” or “measured your food,” matching the Qurʾanic construction; other dialects add “for you.”
TABRISI:83:1-3/r7.anchor: وأهل الحجاز يقولون وزنتك حقك وكلتك طعامك وعليه جاء التنزيل

TABRISI:83:1-3/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r17.claim: When measuring or weighing for others, they short them; the language allows either a direct object or “for them.”
TABRISI:83:1-3/r17.anchor: أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

TABRISI:83:1-3/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:83:1-3/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿūd compares prayer to a measure: whoever fills it is repaid fully by God, while the warning against defrauding is familiar.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r18.anchor: يروى عن ابن مسعود أنه قال الصلاة مكيال فمن وفى وفى الله له

THALABI:v10p149#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p149#3/r4.claim: The phrase means when they measure or weigh for people; Arabic can say I measured or weighed you to mean I did so for you.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r4.anchor: يقال: وزنتك حقك، وكلتك طعامك بمعنى وزنت لك وكلت لك

THALABI:v10p149#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p149#3/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says using the direct object in this construction is a dialect of the people of the Hijaz and neighboring regions.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: وهي لغة أهل الحجاز ومن جاوزهم

THALABI:v10p149#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r6.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
THALABI:v10p149#3/r6.claim: Isa ibn Umar parses the verbs as two separate words, pausing after measured or weighed and beginning a new clause with they shortchange.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلها حرفين حرفين ويقف على: كالوا ووزنوا

THALABI:v10p149#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r7.speaker: حمزة
THALABI:v10p149#3/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd thinks Hamza may likewise have read the verbs as separate words.

THALABI:v10p149#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v10p149#3/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers joining each verb to its object, citing the written form without an alif and idiomatic Arabic transitive usage.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: والاختيار أن يكون كلمة واحدة من جهتين: إحداهما: الخط

THALABI:v10p149#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p149#3/r9.claim: Yukhsirūn means they reduce or shortchange.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310/r1.claim: The phrasing means they measure or weigh for other people; Arabic can say either that they measured someone the food or measured the food for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310/r1.anchor: أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم تقول: كلتني الطعام، كلتك الطعام، تريد كلت لي، وكلت لك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says this transitive construction is characteristic of speakers in the Hijaz and neighboring areas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r1.anchor: وهذا من كلام أهل الحجاز ومن جاورهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites a line about hunting deliberately as an example for an object that means doing it for someone.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the object pronoun is accusative in expressions such as weigh or measure me this much.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r3.anchor: الكسائي يقول: زني كذا، كلني كذا. كالوهم يكيلونهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say not to pause after kālū: the pronoun is attached as in they struck them; al-Zajjāj rejects treating it as emphasis because the written text would then have an alif before it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز الوقف على كالوا حتى تصل ب"هم" كما تقول: ضربهم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r5.claim: The commentators say the short-measurers reduce what they sell or weigh for others, as in the prohibition against reducing the balance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r5.anchor: المفسرون (3): يريد إذا باعوا وكالوا لغيرهم، أو وزنوا نقصوا في الكيل والوزن

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.claim: Authentic traditions cited by Tabari, Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir place at least the first four verses shortly after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.anchor: However, a number of authentic Traditions make it clear that at least the first four verses were

ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.claim: The condemned demand full measure when receiving from others but give less than their due when measuring or weighing what they owe.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.anchor: give less than what is due! [1]

ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.claim: The warning extends beyond commerce to every practical and moral social relation, including each person's rights, obligations, and possessions.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.anchor: does not, of course, refer only to commercial dealings but touches upon every aspect of social relations, both practical and moral

ELMALILI:83:2-3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r2.claim: When measuring or weighing for those same people, they reduce the amount or otherwise shortchange them; habitual fraud explains their deserving Wail.
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r2.anchor: eksiltirler eksik ölçek veya tartı ile ölçerler veya ölçüşte, tartışta eksik yapar

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Muṭaffifīn supplements al-Infiṭār, sharing its theme and elaborating the division of righteous and defiant people at its end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.anchor: This sūrah  is a supplement to S ūrah al-Infi ṭār

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.claim: Al-Infiṭār reasons from God’s attributes displayed in the human body, while this sūrah reasons from the moral nature God gave people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.anchor: attributes of God that are prominent in man’s physical being

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.claim: Human nature loves justice and good and dislikes injustice and evil; this moral distinction shows that the Creator differentiates the just from the unjust rather than treating them alike.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.anchor: by his very nature man likes justice and what is good

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.claim: People commit injustice when other motives overpower their nature, as shown by the dishonest trader who protests when others cheat him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.anchor: the very person who is dishonest in weighing to others cries out with anguish if others are dishonest with him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this reasoning for the Day of Judgement; the author points to his discussion of 75:14–15.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.anchor: readers can take a look at what I have written under the following verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.claim: Verses 1–6 censure people who demand fair treatment while cheating others; their conduct shows they do not expect to be raised before their Lord for judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.anchor: An expression of regret on people who want

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.claim: Taṭfīf means giving short measure or weight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.anchor: The word !ْ#ْﺗﻄﻔﻴﻒ refers to measuring and weighing less

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.claim: The verse contrasts people who insist on full measure from others with their own dishonesty toward others, exposing a moral inconsistency rather than merely naming a trading practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.anchor: a person is very sensitive and vigilant that others should weigh and measure correctly for him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.claim: Such a cheater knows justice requires the same honesty for both sides; he violates his own nature from selfishness, committing open and mean injustice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.anchor: he in fact goes against his own nature purely being overwhelmed with selfishness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.claim: God placed in people a moral barometer that makes them dislike oppression and like justice; when they oppress, desire or emotion overwhelms their ability to keep balance, not their ability to recognize right and wrong.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.anchor: The real reason, as pointed out above, is because he is so overcome by some desire or emotion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.claim: Thieves, murderers, and adulterers would not want the same harm done to their own households, and even impartially acknowledge that society should protect life, wealth, and integrity for everyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.anchor: Only those people should be members of a society who protect the life, wealth and integrity of others

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.claim: This nature shows that people distinguish good from evil and expect different treatment; God must therefore judge righteous and wrongdoers, and the deniers resist because they wish to evade that outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.anchor: An obvious corollary of this is that the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.claim: Exegetes report that dishonest measuring among the Anṣār occasioned revelation of this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.anchor: While explaining this verse, our exegetes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.claim: The author challenges that report’s setting: the sūrah is Meccan, and dishonest trade was at least as plausible among the Meccan traders as among the agricultural Anṣār.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.claim: Even if the Anṣār had the practice, it was no more prevalent than among the Meccans, who were traders, while the Anṣār’s profession was agriculture; the verse’s main point is innate recognition of justice, which implies judgement and accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.anchor: In fact, there was a much greater chance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.claim: Taffif is reduction, from something tiny and insignificant; a mutaffif cheats by an inconspicuous small amount in weight or measure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.anchor: التطفيف النقصان وأصله من الطفيف وهو النزل الحقير والمطفف الآخذ في وزن أو كيل طفيفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.claim: He says it was revealed in Medina about a man called Abu Juhayna who owned two measures, took with the full one and gave with the short one; it is also said to be the first surah revealed there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: كان بالمدينة رجل يكنى أبا جهينة، له مكيلان، يأخذ بالأوفى ويعطي بالأنقص، فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.claim: He says the warning against short measure was revealed in Medina, where the practice was especially corrupt, and the surah corrected people; another account places revelation between Mecca and Medina to reform them before the Prophet arrived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزل بعضها بمكة، ونزل أمر التطفيف بالمدينة لأنهم كانوا أشد الناس فسادا في هذا المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.claim: The prior surah discussed the blessed, the wretched, and the great Day of Judgment; this surah turns to a particularly contemptible sin, cheating in measure for negligible gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.anchor: والمناسبة بين السورتين ظاهرة. لما ذكر تعالى السعداء والأشقياء ويوم الجزاء وعظم شأن يومه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.claim: When they measure for others, they collect what is due to themselves; when they measure or weigh for others, they make the recipients take less.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.anchor: إذا اكتالوا على الناس: قبضوا لهم، وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم، أقبضوهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r4.claim: Measure and weigh normally take their recipient with لام, which can be omitted so the suffix pronoun becomes a direct object; the measured commodity itself is omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r4.anchor: وكال ووزن مما يتعدى بحرف الجر، فتقول: كلت لك ووزنت لك، ويجوز حذف اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r5.speaker: عيسى، حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r5.claim: They treat the object as omitted and هم as a nominative pronoun reinforcing the subject wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r5.anchor: وعن عيسى وحمزة: المكيل له والموزون له محذوف، وهم ضمير مرفوع تأكيد للضمير المرفوع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r6.claim: He rejects taking هم as a subject pronoun, arguing it would make the sentence about who personally does the weighing rather than the action of cheating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ولا يصح أن يكون ضميرا مرفوعا للمطففين، لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says there is no dissonance: reinforcing the pronoun changes nothing about the action being discussed; the recipient is understood in the second clause and the cheats short only other people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r7.anchor: ولا تنافر فيه بوجه، ولا فرق بين أن يؤكد الضمير وأن لا يؤكد، والحديث واقع في الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r8.claim: Asked why the verse says measure or weigh when they short others, he answers that cheats take by measure to enable overfilling and theft, but use either measure or weight when giving to enable shorting in both ways.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r8.anchor: كأن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r15.claim: يخسرون means to reduce or make short; خسر الرجل is intransitive while أخسره makes another person lose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r15.anchor: ويخسرون معدى بالهمزة، يقال: خسر الرجل وأخسره غيره.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r1.claim: The detached pronoun refers to the people from whom they receive goods: when they measure or weigh for them in a sale, they give short measure or weight.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r1.anchor: والضمير المنفصل في قوله تعالى وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون للناس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r2.claim: Because the verb can mean measure for someone or measure that person's goods, some grammarians posit deletion of a preposition; poetry and a proverb illustrate such deletion, while another analysis supplies the omitted measured goods.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r2.anchor: وجعل غير واحد كاله من باب الحذف والإيصال على أن الأصل كال له فحذف الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r3.claim: Isa ibn Umar and Hamza treat the pronoun as an emphatic subject following the verb's subject, pausing after the two waw letters to clarify that reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r3.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر وحمزة أن المكيل له والموزون له محذوف وهم ضمير مرفوع تأكيد للضمير المرفوع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects reading the pronoun as subject: it would say they exact full measure when buying but cheat only when personally doing the measuring, an incoherent contrast because the passage concerns conduct, not who performs it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري لا يصح كون الضمير مرفوعا للمطففين لأنه يكون المعنى عليه إذا أخذوا من الناس استوفوا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r5.claim: A further objection says subject emphasis does not fit the context, which is not distinguishing them from their servants, and the expected consequence would have a connective fa; the detached-object reading also has support from the written form.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r5.anchor: لأن التأكيد اللفظي يدفعه المقام فليس المراد أن يحقق أن الكيل صدر منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r6.claim: They used measures to take goods because this allowed them to demand full amounts and cheat; when paying they used both measures and weights to shortchange in either way, so the verse mirrors their practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69/r6.anchor: إن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.speaker: صبغة الله الحيدوي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.claim: Sayyid Sibghat Allah al-Haydawi argues that measurement cheating usually removes a negligible amount, whereas a small weighing trick can cost much more because weighed goods tend to be more valuable; mentioning cheating even in measures implies worse theft by weight.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.anchor: السيد صبغة الله الحيدوي في ذلك أنالتطفيف في الكيل يكون بشيء قليل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.claim: Alusi says this does not answer why the verse does not instead say they exact in measures and cheat by weight, which would imply the inverse by a fortiori reasoning; ellipsis could make that an instance of antimetabole-like omission.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.anchor: لا يحسم السؤال لجوازان يقال لم لم يقل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mentioning full measure stands for full weight as well, since buying and selling goods use both measures and weights; al-Tibi explains that one side of the parallel implies the other, which Alusi finds unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل وكذلك إذا اتزنوا استوفوا الوزن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says these merchants buy large quantities at once, commonly measured, then sell smaller lots; sales vary in quantity and buyers choose weight or measure, so both are named when they give goods.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.anchor: وقيل إن المطففين باعة وهم في الغلالب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.claim: Alusi cautions that buying large quantities by measure is not universal: in Baghdad of his day, people weighed everything and did not use measures.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن كون العادة الغالبة أخذ الكثير في الكيل غير مسلم على الإطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.claim: Other exegetes say neither statement specifies the commodity measured or weighed, because the passage condemns misconduct in taking and giving generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.anchor: وعدم التعرض للمكيل والموزون في الصورتين على ما قال غير واحد لأن مساق الكلام لبيان سوء معاملة المطففين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r3.claim: When measuring or weighing for others, they give less; Arabic may directly say I measured or weighed you, just as it may say I did these things for you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r3.anchor: {وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون} أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says Isa ibn Umar parses the verbs and hum as separate words, pausing after kalu or wazanu; Abu Ubayda prefers the unified reading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلهما حرفين يقف على "كالوا ووزنوا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda prefers reading each verb with its object as one word: the manuscripts omit the alif that separated forms would require, and Arabic permits the direct construction kalatuka and wazantuka.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r5.anchor: أبو عبيدة: والاختيار الأول (3) يعني: أن كل واحدة كلمة واحدة لأنهم كتبوها بغير ألف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r6.claim: Yukhsirun means they reduce or shortchange.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r7.speaker: نافع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r7.claim: Nafi says Ibn Umar warned merchants to fear God and give full measure and weight, because short-measurers stand at Resurrection sweating to halfway up their ears.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r7.anchor: قال نافع: كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r1.claim: When they measure or weigh for people, the preposition is omitted and the verb made transitive, as supported by the cited poetry.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r1.anchor: أي إذا كالوا الناس أو وزنوا لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r2.claim: Alternatively, the omitted object is their measured amount; treating the separate pronoun as emphasis for the attached pronoun disrupts the contrast of taking and giving and conflicts with Qur'anic spelling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r2.anchor: ولا يحسن جعل المنفصل تأكيدا للمتصل فإنه يخرج الكلام عن مقابلة ما قبله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r11.claim: When measuring or weighing for others, they reduce the amount owed; the object pronoun refers to customers’ due rights, and the wording foregrounds the recipient’s presence and the fraudsters’ habitual shamelessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r11.anchor: أي كالوا الناس أي حقهم أي ما لهم من الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r12.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r12.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar treats kālūhum and wazanūhum as two words each, pausing after the verb and beginning with hum.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r12.anchor: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلهما حرفين يقف على كالوا ووزنوا ويبتدئ هم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah prefers treating each verb and object pronoun as one written word, as supported by the codex spelling without an alif after the plural wāw.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects taking hum as the object pronoun for the customers, arguing that it produces incoherent syntax and shifts the topic from the act to its agent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r14.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون ضميرا للمطففين لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r15.claim: The author counters al-Zamakhsharī: the codex spelling supports the semantic reading that fraudsters take full or extra measure but give customers less.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r15.anchor: ولا شك أن في خط المصحف تقوية لهذا الوجه المعنوي وتأكيدا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r8.speaker: حميد بن ثور
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r8.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Thawr’s poem leaves its referent implicit: وصهباء منها means a tawny she-camel among camels.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r8.anchor:
قال حميد بن ثور في أول قصيدة :
وصهباء منها كالسفينة نضجت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r9.speaker: حاتم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r9.claim: Ḥātim’s line uses بها with an omitted referent, the soul: “when the soul rattles.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r9.anchor:
وقال حاتم :
أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r10.speaker: لبيد
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r10.claim: Labīd’s line means the sun began to set; the sun is unstated and كافر evokes the covering darkness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r10.anchor:
وقال لبيد :
حتى إذا ألقت يدا في كافر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r11.speaker: طرفة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r11.claim: In Ṭarafa’s line, منها refers to the omitted wasteland: “I wish I could ransom you from the desert.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r11.anchor:
وقال طرفة :
ألا ليتني أفديك منها وأفتدي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r12.speaker: الفراء
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the omitted complement as السفه: the fool runs toward folly when restrained.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r12.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء :
إذا نهي السفيه جرى إليه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r14.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r14.speaker: المثقب العبدي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites al-Muthaqib al-ʿAbdī, who alludes to evil alongside good before explicitly naming evil in the next line.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r14.anchor:
قال الفراء: ومثله قول المثقب العبدي :
فما أدري إذا يممت أرضا ... أريد الخير: أيهما يليني؟

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r15.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r15.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r15.claim: In كالواهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون, the omitted preposition ل is restored: they measure or weigh goods for other people.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r15.anchor: وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون (3) [المطففين: 3] أي: كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r2.claim: The verbs كال and وزن normally take a direct object or a lām, which may also be omitted; the idioms كال له and وزن له are possible.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r2.anchor: فعل كال وفعل وزن الأصل أن يتعدى بنفسه أو باللام وممكن الحذف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r3.claim: The lām originally conveys entitlement; omitting it in كالوهم reflects the defrauders' withholding people's due and wronging them.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r3.anchor: فحذف لام الإستحقاق فقال كالوهم لأنهم ظلموا الناس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r4.claim: The verbs could take a direct object or liʾl-istihqāq; omitting the entitlement lām in kalūhum/wazanūhum depicts their refusal to give people their due.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r4.anchor: اللام هنا تفيد الإستحقاق في أصل معناها في اللغة ثم تتشعب إلى معاني متعددة أخرى لكن هؤلاء المطففين لم يعطوا الناس حقوقهم

NASHR:v2p155/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p155/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p155/r1.claim: The established recitation practice does not split words written together when pausing unless a sound transmission permits it; the author regards this as the sounder rule.
NASHR:v2p155/r1.anchor: جميع ما كتب موصولا لا يقطع وقفا إلا برواية صحيحة

NASHR:v2p155/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p155/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p155/r4.claim: Although al-Kisai's permissiveness follows meaning and Khalaf regards script-following as preferable, the author says splitting joined forms is not established among precision readers.
NASHR:v2p155/r4.anchor: وذلك غير معمول به عند أهل الإتقان، ولا معول عليه عند أئمة التحقيق

NASHR:v2p155/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p155/r5.speaker: الأعمش عن أبي بكر عن عاصم، وسورة عن الكسائي
NASHR:v2p155/r5.claim: Al-A'mash from Abu Bakr from Asim and Surah from al-Kisai treat كالوهم أو وزنوهم as one word; al-Dani links this to Nafi's adherence to the written text.
NASHR:v2p155/r5.anchor: روى الأعمش عن أبي بكر عن عاصم كالوهم، أو وزنوهم حرفا واحدا

NASHR:v2p155/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p155/r6.speaker: حمزة عن عبد الله بن صالح العجلي
NASHR:v2p155/r6.claim: A two-word treatment is reported from Hamza only through Abd Allah ibn Salih al-Ajli; al-Dani says performance specialists oppose it, and the author cites their consensus.
NASHR:v2p155/r6.anchor: ثم روى عن حمزة بجعلهما حرفين ثم قال الداني: ولا أعلم أحدا روى ذلك عن حمزة

NASHR:v2p155/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p155/r7.speaker: الجعبري
NASHR:v2p155/r7.claim: Al-Ja'bari says one may pause after each independent word, but on two connected words one pauses after the second; choose the stopping point according to whether the aim is spelling or linguistic origin.
NASHR:v2p155/r7.anchor: وجه الوقف على كل من المنفصل أصالة الاستقلال ووجه منع الوقف على المتصل آخرها التنبيه على وضع الخط

BURHAN:v3p165/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.claim: The author rejects the preceding analysis of كالوهم and وزنوهم on two grounds: the spelling lacks the alif expected by that reading, and الناس shows that the pronoun refers to the people; thus they take full measure from people but give people short measure.
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.anchor: والثاني أن تقدم ذكر الناس يدل على أن الضمير راجع إليهم
